content: SQLite autocommit wraps every statement in its own transaction, so N individual inserts pay N commits/fsyncs (classic benchmark: 5000 inserts 46.9s individually vs 0.047s inside one transaction). Batch writes should open one explicit transaction, prepare the upsert statement once (tx.PrepareContext), loop the binds, and commit once. Default BEGIN is DEFERRED: the write lock is only taken at the first write statement, so two connections that BEGIN, read, then write can hit SQLITE_BUSY on upgrade; BEGIN IMMEDIATE acquires the write lock at BEGIN so writers serialize through busy_timeout instead of racing. modernc exposes this as DSN _txlock=immediate, which rewrites the BEGIN that database/sql emits. Go database/sql has DB.Prepare (lazily re-prepared per connection) and Tx.Prepare (statement tied to one transaction, valid until it ends).
